subject.title: Feature: Include trusted sender_name in inbound metadata envelope

question: Should the trusted inbound envelope expose a human-readable sender display name, or only expose canonical principals derived from stable channel IDs, `session.identityLinks`, or operator-attested provenance?
rationale: Current main deliberately keeps human names out of trusted system metadata, while the open candidate PRs propose different authority models for the same security-sensitive identity gap.

options.title: Prefer canonical principal
options.body: Expose `sender_principal` or `requester_identity` only when a stable provider id matches configured identity links or operator attestation, while keeping display names untrusted.

options.title: Allow trusted display name
options.body: Permit a resolved `sender_display_name` only with channel-specific directory proof, privacy rules, and tests showing spoofable display metadata is not trusted.

options.title: Defer the envelope change
options.body: Keep the current registry workaround until maintainers choose the trusted identity authority and converge the related PRs.

recommendation.title: Prefer canonical principal
recommendation.body: Expose `sender_principal` or `requester_identity` only when a stable provider id matches configured identity links or operator attestation, while keeping display names untrusted.

likelyOwner.reason: Their open identity-links PR is the most complete current candidate for the canonical-principal direction and touches the core metadata boundary.
